vignette: A child is receiving immunosuppressive therapy for a systemic illness. The child now has periodontal problems that began during treatment.
stem: Which interpretation best reflects current guidance on systemic contributors to this child's periodontal findings?

options.text: Immunosuppressive therapy can itself be a contributor to treatment-related periodontal problems.
Immunosuppressive therapy has no effect on the periodontium, so the cause must lie elsewhere.
Diabetes is the only systemic condition recognized as negatively affecting the periodontium.
Medical management of a systemic condition never adds to the child's oral health risks.
